b_a_method: daemon status hook_controlled (observed + hotPathTailAllowance), p99 gated against obs.Budgets() B-A's limit (reported, not gated, under --under-coload — see the notes); see the B-A_spawn_estimate row for the wall-clock, floor-subtracted diagnostic (unbiased at p50, dispersion-contaminated at p99 — spec step 6 amended by controller ruling #29)
notes: B-C not measured in wave 1: the processing seams are stubs

hook_ack_rtt is REPORTED, never gated: it is the client-side ACK round trip of 64 in-process observe.tool deliveries, each with a fresh nonce and a real lease, timed through the same ipc.Client a hook uses. Design §7.5 sizes the ACK deadline from it as AckDeadlineMs = L0IngestMs + ceil(slack99), where slack99 = p99(hook_ack_rtt) - p99(B-B) over this same run. The timed samples are preceded by 2 DISCARDED warm-up requests on the same session: without them sample #0 paid a session-registry insertion and a WAL segment create on top of the round trip, and at 64 samples with nearest-rank percentiles p99 IS the maximum sample, so that one sample became the number the deadline was sized from. Its traffic IS real hot-path traffic, so all 66 requests do reach the daemon's l0_ingest and hook_controlled histograms — but this run reads both of those for the gated B-A and B-B rows BEFORE any of the tranche is sent, warm-ups included, so none of it is inside either gated population, and the B-B this row is differenced against contains none of its own deliveries. They are reconciled rather than ignored: a second status read after the tranche counts every one of them, warm-ups included, into the delivery ledger, so a deferral of this tranche's own cannot pass unnoticed. The in-process traffic that does sit inside the gated populations is the warm-up's, disclosed with its own computed proportion. A p99 over 64 samples is still that set's own top sample, which is why §7.5 takes the maximum across three runs rather than trusting one

daemon-observed hook_controlled_observed (recvTS-reqTS, strict lower bound, no hotPathTailAllowance): p50=3.072ms p99=6.144ms n=5064 — informational cross-check against the gated B-A row above, which adds the tail allowance

B-A's gated n=5064 includes 64 in-process warm-up observe.tool requests (Send-time TS, not a spawned process's main() entry) alongside 5000 real hook spawns from the B-A/B-D loop — the warm-up hot-path tranche (warmHotTranche=64, a small, fixed constant) is 1.3% of the gated population for this run; see B-A_spawn_estimate for the wall-clock diagnostic derived purely from real spawns

B-B's n includes the 64 warm-up hot-path (observe.tool) requests, not just the B-A/B-D measurement loop — the daemon's own l0_ingest count, reported verbatim (conservative for B-B: warm-up payloads run 4KB-256KB, larger than B-A/B-D's fixed representative payload).
